note: Single source of truth for the experiment. server.js builds llms.txt, sitemap.xml and llms-full.txt from this file, so an arm cannot leak into a channel by hand-editing mistake.

arms.title: How long request logs are kept
arms.description: The retention window for this experiment's raw request log, and what is stripped before anything is published.
arms.tests: Is llms.txt alone enough for an agent to find a page that nothing links to?

arms.title: Crawler policy and rate limits
arms.description: Which crawlers are welcome here and how fast they may go.
arms.tests: Does sitemap.xml alone surface a markdown page, with no llms.txt entry?

arms.title: When probes are run

arms.tests: Does listing a page in both channels beat listing it in one?

arms.title: Unlisted control
arms.tests: Control. Listed nowhere, linked nowhere, slug not guessable. A hit here means something outside the designed channels found it.

arms.title: Guessable control
arms.tests: Control. Listed nowhere, but the slug is one agents routinely guess. Separates path guessing from real discovery.

arms.title: Response time on questions about this experiment
arms.description: How quickly a question sent about this experiment gets answered, and what gets answered publicly.
arms.tests: Format control for arm A. Identical treatment, HTML instead of markdown. If F is found and A is not, the format is the problem rather than the linking.
